answer: Under hardware-attested single-seed minting, each identity joining the haven network must present an attestation from a secure element whose embedded key is cryptographically bound to certify exactly one identity ever, and the violet registry records each attestation key's hash permanently. An attacker running a comet-style swarm of fake agents must purchase distinct physical chips per Sybil, so one thousand identities cost roughly one thousand chips, around $8 each, plus procurement logistics that scale linearly or worse with supply constraints.
